Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Aisha Conte (Redwood CSM), Marta Alvarez (Clearwave Head of MLOps), Devon Price (Clearwave Platform Eng), Eric Zhou (CTO), Rina Patel (SRE)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: okay everyone, thanks for joining, um let's do quick intros and then dive into the latency triage and cost reconciliation, we have about 55 minutes so we'll try to keep tight
[00:08] Marta Alvarez: hi all, Marta here, thanks. we've seen p95 spikes during peak queries for our recommendations endpoint, and cost is creeping above forecast so want to understand levers
[00:15] Priya Rao: thanks Marta, quick context question — are those spikes correlated with longer sequences or just concurrency?
[00:22] Devon Price: mostly concurrency — we saw a concurrent burst around 11am PST last week, sequences are typical lengths, not long. p50 stable, p95 jumps to 1.1s from baseline 420ms
[00:33] Priya Rao: got it, concurrency. two immediate levers we usually look at: batching configuration and prefix/KV cache usage — also check if requests are hitting a cold KV cache
[00:44] Eric Zhou: also curious about Dedicated — if we reserve a pool will that flatten p95 or just reduce variability?
[00:51] Jordan Kim: dedicated helps with predictability and tail latency because you own the pool, less noisy neighbors. but cost delta matters — we model that in pilot pricing. hosted with autoscale + burst can work too but you trade some tail risk
[01:05] Rina Patel: quick note — security: we need KMS for key management and audit logs for every tokenized request, SOC 2 is table stakes. can Redwood's Private do on-prem KMS?
[01:15] Priya Rao: yes Private supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem deployment options; we also provide audit log exports. we'll attach security matrix after this call
[01:24] Marta Alvarez: good. can you run us through what you'd change for batching? specifics — window, token thresholds, and any risk to latency SLOs
[01:32] Priya Rao: sure. for concurrency bursts, increase batch window slightly and enable dynamic batching with a max wait of 8ms and a token cap per batch — if p95 is sensitive, we recommend conservative batching at first: max wait 6-8ms and aggressive KV cache usage which avoids repeated prefix work
[01:50] Devon Price: KV cache — is that per customer or per model instance? we've got multiple model variants during rollouts
[01:58] Priya Rao: KV cache is per model instance but you can configure cache warming and shared prefix hints for compatible variants; for rollouts we often pin canary instances to warm caches ahead of traffic
[02:10] Jordan Kim: just to add, we also have quantization profiles that reduce per-token latency slightly and token cost substantially for your high-volume routes — there's a quality vs cost tradeoff we can benchmark
[02:21] Marta Alvarez: hmm quality impact — we need to keep our recommendation accuracy above 96% of baseline, otherwise product team will push back
[02:28] Priya Rao: understood. we'll scope ab test variants: baseline float model, int8 quantized, and a mixed profile. measure both latency and recommendation metric delta on your eval set
[02:39] Eric Zhou: about rollouts — can Redwood automate fallback to a cheaper variant on errors or latency? we want graceful degradation not full outages
[02:47] Jordan Kim: yes we can configure smart routing and fallback policies: if a variant exceeds latency SLO or errors spike, route to a compatible model variant or lower-cost replica. canary -> A/B -> fallback paths are all supported in rollout configs
[03:00] Marta Alvarez: ok sounds good. next on cost — our bill for last month was 34% over forecast, mostly token generation. what levers do we have aside from quantization?
[03:09] Priya Rao: caching (prefix + response caching for deterministic outputs), route-level limits, and adaptive batching. also model selection — a smaller family model for high-volume low-complexity routes. we'd review per-route dashboards to find high spend endpoints
[03:20] Devon Price: we have a heavy rerank route and a short-answer route — rerank is expensive. can we split rerank to smaller model that only runs top-k?
[03:29] Priya Rao: yes, you can do cascaded rerank: lightweight model to filter, heavy model for final top-3. Redwood Console supports tracing so you can see token breakdowns by route
[03:37] Rina Patel: on compliance — are audit logs immutable and how long retained by default? we might need 1 year retention for certain audits
[03:44] Priya Rao: audit logs are write-once in the control plane and you can export to your S3 with lifecycle rules. default retention is 90 days but enterprise packages support longer retention and log archiving
[03:54] Jordan Kim: quick interruption — Devon, can you share sample QPS distribution after the call? that'll help Priya size batching and dedicated capacity modeling
[04:02] Devon Price: yes I'll drop hourly QPS and peak 5-min windows, and also the payload size distributions.
[04:07] Marta Alvarez: timeline — we're aiming for a pilot by mid-June, does that align? we want 30-day pilot to measure p95 improvements and cost per request delta
[04:15] Jordan Kim: mid-June is reasonable. propose pilot scope: 2-week benchmark, then 30-day user-facing pilot on 10% traffic. success criteria: p95 below 600ms for recommendations, <=10% cost uplift vs baseline, and recommendation accuracy within 96% of baseline
[04:30] Eric Zhou: those metrics make sense. how do we instrument rollout? needs to be low-risk and observable
[04:36] Priya Rao: we'll provide a rollout plan doc with tracing hooks, per-route dashboards, and a canary threshold that automatically pauses rollout on error or latency regressions. we'll also recommend a shadow traffic run before live canary
[04:48] Marta Alvarez: about Dedicated vs Hosted — cost differences? do you have a model that shows break-even at our QPS?
[04:55] Jordan Kim: yes Priya will run a cost model. quick rule: if sustained p50/p95 need low variance and you have predictably high sustained QPS, Dedicated often wins on predictable unit cost; Hosted is better for variable traffic and no infra commitments
[05:09] Priya Rao: action item for us: we'll prepare three scenarios — hosted autoscale, dedicated reserved (monthly commit), and private (VPC) with expected unit economics and latency curves.
[05:17] Rina Patel: private deployment question — data residency: can you guarantee customer data never leaves our VPC?
[05:23] Priya Rao: Private option runs a customer-managed control plane and data plane in your VPC or on-prem; we can provide architecture diagrams. we'll include on-prem KMS notes for your security team
[05:31] Marta Alvarez: thanks. one operational quirk, last week's spike correlated with a nightly batch that increased concurrent requests briefly — we can throttle that, but want Redwood to handle short spikes gracefully
[05:40] Priya Rao: we can recommend burst capacity config and autoscale cooldowns — also recommend priority routing for business-critical requests during spikes
[05:48] Jordan Kim: okay let's capture next steps and owners — Sarah (actually Aisha) will draft success criteria and acceptance tests, Devon sends traffic data, Priya preps config and cost scenarios, Jordan sends pilot pricing
[05:58] Devon Price: quick clarification — for benchmarks will we run with our keys in staging or use Redwood test keys?
[06:05] Priya Rao: for accurate latency, use your staging keys and network path; we can run with a temporary pilot account or connect your staging VPC for Private testing
[06:14] Marta Alvarez: perfect. also please include a checklist for required approvals from our infra and security teams so we can route it
[06:20] Aisha Conte: noted, we'll include an approvals checklist and a contact list for escalation
[06:25] Jordan Kim: any other questions before we recap?
[06:28] Eric Zhou: none from me
[06:30] Marta Alvarez: all good
[06:32] Jordan Kim: recap: 1) Jordan to send pilot pricing and simple cost model (due 2026-05-08). 2) Priya to prepare batching, KV cache, and quantization plan plus three deployment scenarios (due 2026-05-12). 3) Devon to upload traffic and payload profiles (due 2026-05-10). 4) Aisha to draft pilot success criteria and approvals checklist (due 2026-05-11). 5) Schedule benchmark window week of 2026-05-18 — Jordan will send calendar invite.
[06:53] Marta Alvarez: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick triage. we'll review the docs and get the internal approvals started
[06:58] Jordan Kim: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the docs and links: docs.redwood.ai/pilot-plan (shared), shared: pilot-pricing.xlsx, and security: redwood.com/security/soc2-summary (placeholder). Meeting adjourned.
